description: Phase 6bx gate — sqllogictest rendering is driven by the typechar declared in `typestring`, NOT by the runtime type of the cell. Mainline sqllogictest coerces TEXT values to integer (atoi prefix-parse; non-numeric prefix → 0) for `I`-typed columns, and to float (atof; non-numeric → 0.000) for `R`-typed columns. This rule was implicit in our spec pre-6bx and the runner was passing TEXT through as-is, causing 22 files in index/random/* (corpus v2) to produce got-hash `acd660ea...` / `dca4e74b...` while mainline expected `b833e3a3...` (10× `0\n`). Engine semantics for the corpus queries are themselves correct — unary `+` on a TEXT value yields the same TEXT value at the engine layer (these cases below verify that). The coercion lives in the runner's `render_value`; this fixture pins the engine-level SQL behavior that feeds into it. Also pins the spec's § `Expected result format` rules for typechar-driven rendering (2026-04-20).

cases.name: unary-plus-on-text-preserves-text
cases.description: Engine returns TEXT as-is when unary `+` is applied to a TEXT column. sqllogictest runner is responsible for the I/R coercion on the expected-output side.

program.sql: SELECT +c FROM t ORDER BY c;

cases.name: text-in-integer-column-not-coerced-by-engine
cases.description: When a column is declared INTEGER but holds a TEXT value (SQLite type affinity is a hint, not a constraint), the engine preserves TEXT. The runner's I-rendering does the coercion.

cases.name: is-not-null-passes-through-text-rows
cases.description: Mirrors the corpus query shape `SELECT col2 FROM t WHERE col3 IS NOT NULL` where col2 is TEXT. Engine returns the TEXT values; runner's type-driven rendering turns them into `0` under `query I` and into the text itself under `query T`.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE tab0(pk INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, col2 TEXT, col3 INTEGER);
SELECT col2 FROM tab0 WHERE col3 IS NOT NULL ORDER BY col2;

cases.name: mixed-col-select-text-and-integer
cases.description: Corpus shape: `SELECT col5 AS col2, 13 AS col0, col3 FROM tab0` — first column TEXT, second/third INTEGER. Engine returns values in their native types; `query III` renders first col as coerced-to-0 via atoi.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE tab0(pk INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, col3 INTEGER, col5 TEXT);
